title: [Keyboard Manager] Backup/restore omits editorSettings.json, leaving new editor settings stale
author: Alb11747

judgment.rationale: The issue includes a before/after configuration comparison, a restore log showing default.json was restored, and a deterministic test showing editorSettings.json matches none of the installed include patterns. Current main still uses case-sensitive Regex.IsMatch and omits an explicit editorSettings rule. One untested save-after-restore path merits a maintainer reproduction before implementation.
evidence: The runtime default.json was restored from the backup while the existing editorSettings.json retained older launch arguments and options.
The extracted backup manifest lists default.json but not editorSettings.json.
The reporter tested the installed include patterns and found that the capital S in editorSettings.json does not match the lowercase *settings.json rule under the current case-sensitive regex.
The issue's only comment is an automated triage summary; it does not add evidence that the stale editor state was reconciled.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the split-state restore and validate a coordinated backup/restore plan before approval.

fix_assessment.rationale: Current backup rules still exclude editorSettings.json, and the reporter's deterministic filter test identifies a PowerToys-owned gap. Restore semantics must keep the editor and runtime representations consistent.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep Keyboard Manager editor and runtime settings aligned during restore
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The backup include patterns contain Keyboard Manager/default.json and lowercase *settings.json. The case-sensitive matching used by IsIncludeFile does not include the camel-cased editorSettings.json, so restore replaces runtime mappings while leaving an existing editor configuration stale.
plan: Reproduce restore onto a destination with an existing new-editor configuration and verify whether a subsequent editor save can overwrite the restored runtime mapping.

Define a coordinated restore rule for Keyboard Manager/default.json and editorSettings.json so both representations are restored or reconciled together; avoid merely adding the file without deciding how older backups and existing destinations are handled.
Add backup/restore tests for the camel-cased filename, existing-destination restore, and post-restore editor/runtime consistency.
verification: Run focused Settings.UI.Library backup/restore tests proving editorSettings.json is selected by the intended rule and that a destination restore does not leave conflicting Keyboard Manager values.
Repeat the reporter's restore scenario, reopen the new editor, save the affected mapping, and confirm runtime arguments and launch options remain the restored values.

confidence.rationale: Current source and the reporter's filter experiment support the omission cause, but a clean reproduction is needed to establish the safest treatment of existing editor state and the subsequent-save risk.

issue_context.summary: Restoring a PowerToys backup updates Keyboard Manager's runtime mapping file but leaves the new editor's separately persisted settings at their pre-restore values.
known_information: The reporter tested PowerToys 0.101.2362 with the new editor enabled and included a sanitized evidence ZIP.
The restore log records Keyboard Manager/default.json being updated, and the runtime subsequently launches Chrome with the restored arguments.
The existing editorSettings.json retained older values and timestamp; the extracted backup manifest did not contain that file.
Current main's SettingsBackupAndRestoreUtils.IsIncludeFile uses Regex.IsMatch without IgnoreCase, and backup_restore_settings.json has no explicit editorSettings.json include rule.
inferences: The case-sensitive include-pattern mismatch plausibly explains why editorSettings.json is omitted.
A later editor save could restore stale values into the runtime configuration, but the reporter has not tested that overwrite path.
issue_context.analysis: The report establishes a split between a successfully restored runtime file and stale editor state. The source-level filter explains the omission; before selecting a safe fix, a maintainer should verify the post-restore save path and ensure older backups do not replace valid editor data with an absent or incompatible file.
initial_investigation: Inspected current main's SettingsBackupAndRestoreUtils.IsIncludeFile/GetSettingsFiles and backup_restore_settings.json: matching is case-sensitive and the include list contains default.json but no editorSettings.json.
Reviewed the reporter's deterministic wildcard test, restore log, and table of old editor values versus restored runtime values.
The one issue comment is an automated triage summary; it adds no further repro or fix evidence.

actions.note: The include-rule mismatch is demonstrated; confirm existing-destination and subsequent-save behavior before implementation.

reproduce.title: Verify Keyboard Manager editor/runtime state after restore
reproduce.version_requirement: PowerToys 0.101.2362 with the new editor enabled, as reported
prerequisites: Use a test profile with a global Open app shortcut whose Chrome arguments and launch options differ between default.json and editorSettings.json.
Create a backup containing the runtime default.json and restore it over a destination that already has editorSettings.json.
steps: Record the shortcut arguments and launch options in both files before restore.
Restore the backup and confirm which files are written and which values remain in the new editor.
Open Keyboard Manager, inspect the affected shortcut, save it without unrelated edits, and restart or invoke the shortcut to compare the resulting runtime values.
Repeat with a destination that has no editorSettings.json to check the legacy-backup and first-run behavior.
reproduce.expected_result: After restore, the editor and runtime representations agree, and saving the editor does not replace restored values with stale destination settings.
reproduce.actual_to_confirm: Whether the stale editor values survive restore and overwrite the restored runtime mapping on a later editor save.

status.label: Reproduce restore consistency
status.detail: The filename filter mismatch is supported by current source; verify restore behavior with an existing editor file before choosing reconciliation semantics.
